**Centroids ($\mathcal{N}$):** A set of 3D points $n = (n_x, n_y, n_z)$ representing the centers of spatial cells.
**Submodules ($f^n$):** For each centroid $n$, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) containing fully connected layers.

Tessellate the scene into a top-down 2D grid.
Initialize a set of MLP weights $\{f^n\}$, one for each centroid $n \in \mathcal{N}$.
Sample points along the camera rays corresponding to each pixel.
Identify which spatial cells these rays intersect.
Assign the pixel to the trainset $\mathcal{T}_n$ only for those intersecting cells $n$.
Use the coarse geometry inferred by the NeRFs to identify occluders.
